text: Nilotinib is a second-generation tyrosine kinase inhibitor designed to bind with high affinity to the inactive conformation of the BCR-ABL1 fusion protein, the constitutively active kinase driving Chronic Myeloid Leukemia (CML). By occupying the ATP-binding pocket of the ABL1 domain, Nilotinib prevents the phosphorylation of downstream signaling substrates, thereby inhibiting the proliferative and anti-apoptotic pathways essential for leukemic cell survival. Its structural optimization—featuring a more rigid, hydrophobic scaffold compared to Imatinib—enhances binding potency and selectivity, allowing it to overcome many Imatinib-resistant mutations and effectively induce apoptosis in BCR-ABL1-positive cells.
